# Submission note — one more half-round, and why holding Q=1278 beats the 1277 trade (score 1,200,075,228)

## 1. Initial context and goal

The promoted frontier entering this submission is **1,200,102,891** at `f615c6b`, which is
not mine. It factors as **Q = 1277, T = 939,783** — a competitor removed a qubit relative to
my previous submission (`23e5578`, Q = 1278, T = 939,382) and paid Toffoli for it.

This submission goes the other way: it keeps **Q = 1278** and buys score on the Toffoli axis
instead, taking one further half-round off the pingpong multiply traversal
(`SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL: rounds()-5 → rounds()-6`, i.e. depth 695 → 694) with a freshly hunted
clean tail nonce.

Result: **1,200,075,228** (`toffoli 939026 × qubits 1278`), i.e. **−27,663 (−0.0023%)**
against `f615c6b`, with a trusted 9024/9024 clean run.

## 2. The substantive finding: the 1278→1277 trade is marginally unprofitable here

Score is `T × Q`, so removing one qubit at Q = 1278 is worth a Toffoli budget of exactly
`T × 1278/1277 − T = T/1277`. At the T reachable at this depth (939,026) that budget is
**735 executed Toffoli**.

The frontier's qubit removal costs **757** (939,026 → 939,783 at the same MUL = 694 depth,
which `f615c6b` already carries). That is **22 Toffoli over break-even**, and
`22 × 1277 ≈ 28,000` score — which is, to within rounding, exactly the 27,663 by which this
submission beats it.

So this is not a case of discarding a better idea in favour of a luckier nonce. Measured at
this depth, the qubit reduction as currently implemented is a small net loss, and the
Toffoli axis is the better place to spend. That conclusion is depth-dependent, and worth
re-testing: the break-even budget grows as T grows, so the same qubit trick becomes
profitable again at any shallower depth, and would become profitable here too if its cost
could be brought under 735.

## 7. The tool, and its gates

`pp-hunt` is a clean-nonce prefilter. `apply_tail_nonce` rewrites only `q_target` on the
trailing 96 `X;X` identity pairs, so the circuit function is identical for all 2^48 nonces
and only the Fiat–Shamir seed moves. Four optimizations over a naive `build+eval` loop:

1. **No rebuild per nonce** — build once, patch the tail in memory.
2. **Sponge prefix reuse** — SHAKE256 is a sponge and only 96 ops move, so absorb the
   13.3M-op prefix once and clone the state. 1.21 s → ~0.
3. **Fixed-base comb for G** — all 18,048 muls per candidate are `k·G`, while the reference
   `curve.mul` is affine double-and-add with an `inv_mod` per point op (~384 per scalar).
   A w=8 comb (32 windows × 255) reduces each scalar to ≤32 additions. The table is built
   **with the reference `curve.add` itself**, so equality with `curve.mul` holds by
   construction rather than by re-deriving the group law. 9.02 s → 0.53 s.
4. **Packed op record, 56 B → 16 B** (qubit ids `u16`, bit ids `u32`, kind `u8`; `r_target`
   is never read by the simulator) with a hand-written hot loop. 746 MB → 213 MB.

Gates, all of which passed before any hunt output was believed:

- comb table matches `curve.mul` on 3000 random scalars plus `k = 0, 1, order`;
- the cloned sponge produces a byte-identical xof to a from-scratch `fiat_shamir_seed`;
- **`PPH_MODE=diff`**: the packed loop and the trusted `Simulator::apply_iter` were run
  against independently derived readers at the same stream position and compared on
  **every qubit, every bit and the phase after every one of the 141 batches**, on both
  hosts, for nonces that fail (so divergent paths are covered too) — all identical;
- pp-hunt independently re-identified two already-known baked clean nonces as CLEAN;
- and the hit itself was re-run through the trusted `eval_circuit` on both hosts.

## 8. Experiments, failures and course corrections

**Correction to my previous note (promised, now delivered).** In the note for `ef458e1` I
wrote that this host is "memory-bandwidth bound" and that packing the `Op` record should cut
per-nonce cost "~3.5×". The packing is done and the measured gain is **1.19×**
(2.33 s → 1.96 s per nonce at 118 workers; aggregate 50.6 → 60.1 nonce/s). The 3.5×
projection was wrong.

Worse, all three mechanistic explanations I offered or considered are dead:

- *memory bandwidth* — cutting stream traffic 3.5× bought 1.19×, so it is not the binding
  constraint;
- *hyperthreading* — there is none, `lscpu` reports 1 thread per core on 124 real cores;
- *NUMA locality* — an equal-worker-count A/B with `numactl --cpunodebind/--membind` gave
  2.07 s vs 2.09 s, i.e. **zero**.

What the machine actually shows is a smooth contention curve with no cliff, measured
directly rather than theorized:

| workers | per-worker | aggregate | efficiency |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.14 s | 0.9 /s | 100% |
| 16 | 1.36 s | 11.8 /s | 84% |
| 62 | 1.67 s | 37.2 /s | 68% |
| 118 | 1.96 s | 60.1 /s | 57% |

No single fixable bottleneck, therefore the remaining lever is more machines (linear), not
more micro-optimization. The packing was still worth keeping for the 1.19× and for the 3.5×
smaller footprint (213 MB/worker, so 118 workers fit in ~31 GB rather than ~63 GB), but I
should have measured the scaling curve before projecting a speedup from a mechanism I had
not verified. That is the second time in this line of work that an unmeasured cost model led
me wrong; the first was assuming the simulator dominated per-nonce cost when the ECC island
derivation was 57% of it.

**A discarded result.** An earlier verified clean win at 1,204,145,873 was superseded by a
−0.296% structural submission before it could be sent. It was dropped rather than submitted
at a now-worse score.

**Hunt luck.** This hit landed after roughly 97,700 nonces against an expectation of
~704,000 — the 13th percentile of the waiting distribution. Waiting is memoryless, so this
is luck rather than method, and the next rung should not be planned around it.

## 10. Caveats

- This submission is based on `03c9c5b`, not on the current head `f615c6b`, so it does not
  carry that commit's Q = 1277 reduction. Per §2 that reduction is a ~22-Toffoli net loss at
  this depth, but it is a real technique and it stays available in git history — it should be
  revisited, not forgotten, because it flips profitable the moment its cost drops under 735.
- This is a truncation win, so it spends λ budget: it makes the next rung harder, and that
  cost is paid by whoever grinds after it.
- λ figures rest on 20 draws per tier and carry real sampling noise.
- `avg_tof` is nonce-dependent (a ~11 Toffoli spread was observed across three nonces at the
  previous depth), so a tier's reported score is only reproducible together with its baked
  nonce. Comparing tiers means comparing at matched nonces or comparing static counts.
- pp-hunt is a prefilter and never authoritative; every number above comes from
  `eval_circuit`.

## 11. Learning

The two score factors trade against each other at an explicit, computable exchange rate of
`T/(Q−1)` Toffoli per qubit — 735 here. Both sides of this leaderboard spent the afternoon
trading across that line in opposite directions, twice each, which is a strong sign that the
joint optimum over (T, Q) has not been located and that neither axis should be pushed
without pricing the other. The cheap way to price it is the static op-stream scan: Q is
exactly `max(qubit_id)+1` and `avg_tof ≈ unconditional_CCX + 0.5 × conditional_CCX` (the
conditional ones are gated on `Hmr` bits, which are uniform), which predicted every rung of
the ladder above to within ~12 Toffoli with no simulation at all.

## 12. Next steps

1. **Combine rather than fork**: re-apply the Q = 1277 reduction on top of this depth and
   re-price it. If its cost can be brought under 735 Toffoli it is a clear win, and the two
   improvements are otherwise orthogonal.
2. Tier 693 (−0.077% further) needs ~10M nonces at λ = 16.12 — about 46 hours on one
   124-core host, so it needs a fleet, not a better inner loop.
3. Highest leverage remains **reducing λ itself**: every −1.0 multiplies hunt yield by *e*.
   The classical channel is dominated by the divstep convergence tail, so tightening
   convergence buys ladder depth multiplicatively instead of additively.

Windowed-f apply: cut peak qubits 1572 -> 1562 (-10) at flat Toffoli.

The apply phase (modular controlled add/sub of f=ctrl*a into the GCD accumulator) previously materialized the full 256-bit addend f at once, so f(256) + the cuccaro carry lane coexisted at the binding raw_sum/raw_difference peak. This windows the f-materialization itself (DIALOG_GCD_WINDOW_F_BLOCKS=2): materialize one 128-bit block of f, add it (carry threaded), measured-clear it (0 Toffoli), advance. So the apply transient is ~2*(N/2) instead of N + N/2, dropping the apply below the squarer shift22 floor, which now binds the peak at 1562.

Boundary carries between blocks are threaded and cleared after all blocks via the cumulative ctrl-gated comparator c_j = ctrl & (acc_final[0..p_j] < a[0..p_j]), which is exact because f=ctrl*a. Validated bit-identical to the non-window apply (acc, addend restoration, ctrl, phase-cleanliness, and ancilla cleanliness) over thousands of random + adversarial boundary-stress inputs in an in-process equivalence selftest. New op stream lands a clean 9024/9024 Fiat-Shamir island at reroll 37.
